table_title: List the 51 WWF Global 200 priority ecoregions of the 'Tropical and Subtropical Moist Broadleaf Forests' major habitat type (TMBF biome), organized by biogeographic realm, per Wikipedia's `Global 200` master article. WWF's Global 200 is a closed canonical curated list of ~238 priority ecoregions identified by World Wildlife Fund as most critical for biodiversity conservation. The TMBF biome subset spans 5 of 8 biogeographic realms (Afrotropical 11 entries, Australasia 8, Indomalaya 18, Neotropic 12, Oceania 2 = 51 total — Palearctic/Nearctic/Antarctic have no TMBF entries because tropical moist broadleaf forests don't exist in those realms). For each parent Global 200 ecoregion entry, give the realm (closed 5-value categorical), semicolon-delimited list of representative WWF child ecoregions listed under the parent in the master, and semicolon-delimited list of WWF ecoregion codes listed next to those child ecoregion labels.
db_analog: SELECT global_200_ecoregion, realm, string_agg(wwf_ecoregion_name, '; ') AS representative_wwf_ecoregions, string_agg(wwf_ecoregion_code, '; ') AS wwf_ecoregion_codes FROM global_200_priority_ecoregions WHERE major_habitat_type = 'Tropical and Subtropical Moist Broadleaf Forests' GROUP BY global_200_ecoregion, realm ORDER BY realm ASC, global_200_ecoregion ASC
temporal_note: Wikipedia `Global 200` master article, accessed 2026-05-18. Universe is the closed canonical 51-entry list of WWF Global 200 priority ecoregions in the 'Tropical and Subtropical Moist Broadleaf Forests' (TMBF) major habitat type per the master article's TMBF section. WWF Global 200 is a closed canonical curated list maintained by World Wildlife Fund since 1997-1998 publication; the TMBF subset is stable. source_count = 1 registered (master article supplies universe membership + Realm + Representative WWF Ecoregions + WWF Ecoregion Codes cell values via its consolidated TMBF-by-realm tabulation). Per cycle-3 audit's master-derived row-list dump: counts are Afrotropical 11 + Australasia 8 + Indomalaya 18 + Neotropic 12 + Oceania 2 = 51 parent Global 200 entries. Per-row cells: Global 200 Ecoregion parent label verbatim from master TMBF section; Realm per master section heading; Representative WWF Ecoregions semicolon-delim child ecoregion labels per master; WWF Ecoregion Codes semicolon-delim per master (Afrotropical AT-prefix; Australasia AA-prefix; Indomalaya IM-prefix; Neotropic NT-prefix; Oceania OC-prefix). temporal_sensitivity = low — WWF Global 200 list is stable; rare revisions. **Replaces abandoned `major_tropical_rainforests_by_continent` design** after 2 rounds of pre-staging design review on that instance exposed structural universe-fuzziness (no closed canonical 'major rainforests' authoritative list); lesson applied here: pivot to closed canonical WWF Global 200 universe with source_defined defensibility.

Single PK Global 200 Ecoregion (parent entry labels unique within the 51-entry universe per master TMBF section). **Brings `geographic` from gap 2 (3 of 5: transboundary_rivers_by_continent_over_1000_km + transboundary_rivers_by_continent_over_100_miles + decade_volcanoes_by_continent) to gap 1 (4 of 5)** — one more saturates as the next fully-cleared category (alongside aggregation, comparative, hierarchical_decomposition, temporal). **Closes the LAST remaining gap-2 category — benchmark milestone**: uniform-gap-1-or-better state across all 15 categories. Environment family extends from 1 to 2 instances (Environment/Energy `countries_over_50pct_renewable_electricity` was the sole prior Environment instance; this brings to 2 with NEW Environment/Conservation subdomain). NEW `physical-features/ecoregions` fine-class extending physical-features bucket from 8 to 9 instances (joining mountains, rivers×2, deserts, islands, oceanic-trenches, lakes, volcanoes). No validation cross-checks registered or documented (per cycle-3 audit's source_count=1 confirmation; per-ecoregion Wikipedia articles exist but are not needed — master tabulation supplies all cells). Mirror precedent for source_count=1 master-only source plan: `decade_volcanoes_by_continent` (16-entry IAVCEI closed list); `phanerozoic_periods_by_start_age` (12-period ICS Phanerozoic universe). claim_type = source_defined — universe is closed canonical 51-entry WWF Global 200 TMBF list maintained by World Wildlife Fund; all 4 cells are source-extractive (master TMBF section row labels for Global 200 Ecoregion; master section headings for Realm; child ecoregion labels listed under each parent for Representative WWF Ecoregions; codes listed next to children for WWF Ecoregion Codes). No curator judgment. Cycle arc: 3 rounds of pre-staging design review (cycle-1 'Revise' with universe-fuzziness on major_tropical_rainforests_by_continent + path-A pivot to Global 200; cycle-2 'Revise' with 4 BLOCKING — granularity / realm vocab / country cell / 4th cell; cycle-3 'Approve With 1 Required Correction' — row count 50→51 with master-derived row-list dump). Cycle-3 audit's specific master-derived dump was used verbatim at cycle-0 staging — all 51 rows × 4 cells master-extracted with NO best-guess values (avoiding decade_volcanoes-style cycle-1 BLOCKING factual catch on 9 cell mismatches). 4-cell schema (Global 200 Ecoregion PK + Realm + Representative WWF Ecoregions + WWF Ecoregion Codes) at 51 rows = 204 source-grounded cell values. Sort: Realm ASC alphabetic (primary) + Global 200 Ecoregion ASC alphabetic (within realm). Confidence gradient: very-LLM-knowable parent entries include Atlantic forests (Brazil iconic Mata Atlântica), Borneo lowland and montane forests (largest SE Asian rainforest), Sumatran Islands (orangutan habitat), Madagascar lowlands and subhumid forests, Greater Antillean moist forests; mid-difficulty include Albertine Rift montane forests (DRC/Uganda/Rwanda mountain gorilla habitat), Eastern Arc Montane Forests (Tanzania endemic), Western Ghats moist forests, Chocó–Darién, Talamancan-Isthmian Pacific; harder calibration include WWF Ecoregion Codes (AT0111 = Eastern Guinean forests; specific 4-digit codes are deeply technical), Indomalaya parent vs child distinctions (Borneo lowland and montane forests parent vs IM0102 Borneo lowland / IM0103 montane / IM0104 peat swamp children), Naga-Manupuri-Chin hills naming (multi-state India/Myanmar mountain region), Maldives–Lakshadweep–Chagos Archipelago tropical moist forests (single child same-name parent). Geographic category-fit: per the geographic category contract, each row is a per-realm listing emphasizing biogeographic distribution. The 5-realm partition with uneven counts (Afrotropical 11 / Australasia 8 / Indomalaya 18 / Neotropic 12 / Oceania 2) reflects the actual geographic concentration of tropical moist broadleaf forests on Earth — Indomalaya (SE Asia + Indian subcontinent) is most-represented because of the high-biodiversity Sundaland + Indochina + Indian Ghats regions; Oceania is least-represented (only South Pacific Islands + Hawaii). This uneven shape distinguishes the instance from hierarchical_decomposition (which would require top-N-per-parent uniformity) and matches the `decade_volcanoes_by_continent` geographic precedent. **Replaces abandoned `major_tropical_rainforests_by_continent`** after 2 rounds of pre-staging on that design exposed structural universe-fuzziness (no closed canonical 'major rainforests' authoritative list); pivot to Global 200 TMBF subset locked source_defined cleanly. 4-cycle audit history total: 3 pre-staging design reviews + cycle-0 staging.
